question: GQ-001
subject: the blast radius I noted twice and never measured
the_pattern: Twice on 2026-08-05 a guard I added broke a suite it was not aimed at. I wrote "every new check has a blast radius" and did nothing about it. Five suites existed and NOTHING ran them together — so each time I added a gate I ran whichever suite I happened to think of.
built: scripts/check-all.sh — npm run check:all, every suite run to completion, no short-circuit
why_no_short_circuit: a chain that stops at the first failure hides HOW MANY things one change broke, which is the number this reports

proven_on_the_real_failure.method: reverted last turn's scratch-copy hook wiring on a copy
proven_on_the_real_failure.result: 2 of 4 suites FAILED — verify chain AND gates load-bearing
proven_on_the_real_failure.what_that_showed: the blast radius was WIDER than the one suite I noticed last turn

timings_that_forced_a_split.gate_selftest: 437s (runs the whole chain once per case, 15 cases)
timings_that_forced_a_split.decision: a gate that makes pushing painful gets bypassed. --quick keeps verify + retention (128s) on every push; the two chain-replaying suites run from npm run check:all by hand.

hook_now_covers_more.now: check-all --quick — verify AND the retention self-test, which verify never touched
hook_now_covers_more.stated_limit: the hook does NOT run gate-selftest or load-bearing; that is written in the hook itself so nobody reads it as covering everything
